extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and advanced undergraduates learning algebraic geometry (readers of Vakil's 'The Rising Sea')
extracted.subtask_description: Textbook chapter material giving definitions, properties, and exercises about associated primes/points, rational functions/total quotient ring, and the definition and basic properties of morphisms of (locally) ringed spaces and schemes. Includes concrete criteria for when maps of schemes arise from ring maps and how to check morphisms via affines or functor-of-points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: associated prime (annihilator) (D)
rubrics_metrics.description: A prime p is said to be associated to an A-module M if p is the annihilator of an element m of M (p = Ann(m) = {a in A : a m = 0}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awkwardly equivalent formulation: p is associated to M iff M has a submodule isomorphic to A/p. Notation: Ass M (or Ass_A M) denotes the set of prime ideals associated to M. (Used throughout to define associated points of schemes.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent characterization of associated primes
rubrics_metrics.description: p ∈ Ass M iff M has a submodule isomorphic to A/p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This equivalence is used repeatedly (e.g., to produce sections supported precisely on an associated point) and is the basis for many exercises proving finiteness and support statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 5.5.10(a): Finiteness and nonemptiness of Ass M (Noetherian case)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is Noetherian and M ≠ 0 is finitely generated, then Ass M is finite and nonempty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is property (B) referenced earlier. Exercise 5.5.J and the composition-series style Exercise 5.5.M supply proofs (filtration with successive quotients A/pi).

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 5.5.10(b): Injectivity of localization map
rubrics_metrics.description: For a Noetherian ring A and finitely generated M ≠ 0, the natural map M → ∏_{p ∈ Ass M} M_p is an injection (cf. (5.5.3.1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows from checking vanishing in localizations at maximal associated primes (Exercise 5.5.K) and is used to establish uniqueness statements (e.g., maximal domain of rational functions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 5.5.10(c): Zerodivisors are union of associated primes
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of zerodivisors of M equals the union ⋃_{p ∈ Ass M} p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One direction is clear: elements in an associated prime annihilate a nonzero element. Conversely, if a annihilates a nonzero element, it is contained in some maximal annihilator ideal which is prime (Exercise 5.5.J).

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 5.5.10(d): Association commutes with localization
rubrics_metrics.description: If S is a multiplicative set, then Ass_{S^{-1}A}(S^{-1}M) = {pS^{-1}A : p ∈ Ass_A M and p ∩ S = ∅}. Equivalently, Ass S^{-1}A S^{-1}M = Ass_A M ∩ Spec S^{-1}A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Important Exercise 5.5.N for the localization argument (use Hom and localization of Hom groups).

rubrics_metrics.name: Associated points are generic points of components (property (A))
rubrics_metrics.description: Every associated point is the generic point of an irreducible component of the support of some element m ∈ M (i.e., an associated point is generic for a component of Supp m).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 5.5.P(a) shows each associated p = Ann(m) is generic point of an irreducible component of Supp m; this ties associated points to geometry (closures of points).

rubrics_metrics.name: Support of an element equals closure of associated points where its germ is nonzero
rubrics_metrics.description: For m ∈ M, the support of m is the closure of those associated points at which m has nonzero germ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 5.5.P(b) (using earlier properties) proves this: localize at p to check vanishing, and use Theorem 5.5.10(b,d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of supports realizable by single elements (Exercise 5.5.O)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsets of Spec A that occur as the support of an element of M are precisely the closures of subsets of the associated points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: for each associated point p there is a section supported exactly on p; combine to get arbitrary closures of subsets of Ass M.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of associated primes via maximal annihilators (Exercise 5.5.J)
rubrics_metrics.description: If I is maximal among proper ideals that are annihilators of elements of M, then I is prime; thus in the Noetherian case Ass M is nonempty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General philosophy: ideals maximal with respect to a property often turn out to be prime. This is used to show existence of associated primes without constructing them explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypersurfaces have no embedded points (Exercise 5.5.I)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f ∈ k[x1,...,xn] is nonzero, then A := k[x1,...,xn]/(f) has no embedded points (i.e., no associated primes other than minimal ones).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: lift a zerodivisor g in A to k[x1,...,xn] and show g has a common factor with f using that k[x1,...,xn] is a Noetherian UFD. This is useful when studying nonreduced hypersurfaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rational function on a locally Noetherian scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: A rational function on a locally Noetherian scheme X is an element of the image of Γ(U,O_X) under the natural map (5.5.5.1) for some open U containing all the associated points; equivalently the colimit of O_X(U) over opens containing the associated points, or an ordered pair (U,f) with U containing all associated points, modulo agreement on overlaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the map (5.5.5.1) is injective, rational functions have a maximal domain of definition. Define regularity: f is regular at p if p lies in that maximal domain. Examples: on Spec k[x,y]/(y^2,xy), x^{-2}/((x-1)(x-3)) is rational with domain excluding x=1,3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total fraction (quotient) ring / function field (5.5.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rational functions on X form a ring called the total fraction ring (total quotient ring) of X; if X = Spec A is affine, this is the total fraction ring of A. If X is integral, this equals the function field K(X) (stalk at the generic point).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This generalizes the notion of fraction field to non-integral schemes; it coincides with earlier definitions in the integral case (Deﬁnition 5.2.H).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal primes give zerodivisors (non-Noetherian remark 5.5.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Even without Noetherian hypotheses: if p is a minimal prime, any element s ∈ p is a zerodivisor in A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: localize at p to see s/1 nilpotent in A_p (unique prime), hence some t s^n = 0 globally, so s is a zerodivisor. Used later (e.g., Exercise 11.1.G).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary decomposition and associated primes (5.5.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: The associated prime ideals of an ideal I are precisely the radicals of ideals occurring in any primary decomposition of I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary ideals I (I primary if xy ∈ I implies x ∈ I or y^n ∈ I) and primary decomposition (Lasker–Noether) produce associated primes as radicals; see standard references such as Eisenbud for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: morphism of ringed spaces (6.2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism of ringed spaces π : X → Y consists of a continuous map of topological spaces π together with a map O_Y → π_* O_X of sheaves of rings (equivalently π^{-1}O_Y → O_X), interpreted as a 'pullback map' on functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By adjointness this is the same as a map π^{-1}O_Y → O_X. Think of it as saying functions on Y pull back to functions on X compatibly with restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open embedding / open immersion of ringed spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: If U ⊂ Y is open and (U, O_Y|_U) is isomorphic to an open subset V ⊂ Y via an isomorphism, then the induced map U → Y is an open embedding (open immersion) of ringed spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formalizes gluing and local checks for morphisms; used frequently when constructing maps by describing them on distinguished opens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gluing of morphisms of ringed spaces (6.2.A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an open cover X = ⋃ U_i and morphisms π_i : U_i → Y that agree on overlaps U_i ∩ U_j, there is a unique morphism π : X → Y restricting to each π_i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the basic local-to-global principle: morphisms can be specified by compatible local data on an open cover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Induced map on stalks (6.2.C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given π : X → Y a morphism of ringed spaces and p ∈ X with π(p)=q, there is an induced map of stalks (O_Y)_q → (O_X)_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maps on stalks are used to track vanishing: pullback sends germs vanishing at q to germs vanishing at p (and is crucial for the locally ringed condition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction: morphism Spec A → Spec B from ring map B → A (Key Ex. 6.2.D)
rubrics_metrics.description: A ring homomorphism π^#: B → A determines a morphism of ringed spaces π : Spec A → Spec B: on distinguished open sets D(g) in Spec B the map on sections is O_{Spec B}(D(g)) = B_g → O_{Spec A}(π^{-1}D(g)) = A_{π^# g} given by localization of π^#.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This three-step construction (map of sets, map of topological spaces, map on sheaves) gives the standard affine-scheme morphism induced by a ring map; check independence of choices of g and sheaf axioms on the distinguished basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not every morphism of ringed spaces between affines arises from a ring map (6.2.E)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exist maps of ringed spaces Spec k(x) → Spec k[y]_{(y)} not arising from a ring map B → A as in Key Ex. 6.2.D; such maps are not morphisms of locally ringed spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This motivates restricting to morphisms of locally ringed spaces when defining morphisms of schemes, to ensure the affine correspondence holds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: morphism of locally ringed spaces (6.3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism of locally ringed spaces π : X → Y is a morphism of ringed spaces such that for each p ∈ X with q = π(p), the induced map on stalks π^#: (O_Y)_q → (O_X)_p is a local homomorphism, i.e., it sends the maximal ideal of (O_Y)_q into the maximal ideal of (O_X)_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intuitively: functions vanishing at q pull back to functions vanishing at p. This property is used to recover the desired correspondence between ring maps and geometric maps on affines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: morphism of schemes (6.3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism of schemes is a morphism of locally ringed spaces. Schemes thus form the category Sch with morphisms defined this way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After defining locally ringed spaces and checking compatibility with affines, this gives the standard category of schemes; one then often checks properties on affine covers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key Proposition 6.3.2: Affine morphisms determined by global sections
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : Spec A → Spec B is a morphism of locally ringed spaces, then it is the morphism induced by the ring map π^#: B = Γ(Spec B, O) → Γ(Spec A, O) = A (i.e., morphisms between affines correspond bijectively to ring maps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof recovers the map on points from which global functions vanish and checks the sheaf map on distinguished opens; this justifies the affine-spectrum/ring correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms to an affine scheme correspond to ring maps (Essential Ex. 6.3.F)
rubrics_metrics.description: Morphisms X → Spec A are in natural bijection with ring morphisms A → Γ(X, O_X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the affine case and gluing. Practical consequence: the canonical morphism X → Spec Γ(X, O_X) exists; it is an isomorphism iff X is affine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical morphism to Spec of global sections and affineness criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a canonical morphism X → Spec Γ(X, O_X); X is affine iff this canonical morphism is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning in text: Γ(X,O_X) might be 'nasty' even for finite-type schemes; affineness is a geometric condition, not automatic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Yoneda-type determination of morphisms via Z-valued points (6.3.L)
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism of schemes X → Y is determined by the induced maps on Z-valued points X(Z) → Y(Z) as Z varies over all schemes (i.e., via the functor of points).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete consequence: the induced maps on A-valued points for all rings A determine the morphism; Exercise 6.3.L(b) points toward Yoneda's Lemma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of morphisms to projective space from functions (6.3.M)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a B-scheme and f_0,...,f_n are n+1 functions on X with no common zeros, then [f_0:...:f_n] gives a morphism X → P^n_B. If g is nowhere vanishing on X, then [f_0:...:f_n] and [g f_0:...:g f_n] define the same morphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a concrete way to produce maps to projective space from global functions without common zeros; the general characterization uses sections of a line bundle (Theorem 16.4.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms from local and residue-field Specs (6.3.J,6.3.K)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are canonical morphisms Spec O_{X,p} → X and Spec κ(p) → X giving p the structure of a scheme-point. For a local ring (A,m), Mor(Spec A, X) bijects with pairs (p ∈ X, local homomorphisms O_{X,p} → A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: maps from local rings land in neighborhoods of a single point p and correspond to local data at that point; useful for understanding A-valued points for local A.
